t: Under the names Jianye, Jiankang, Jiangning and Nanjing, the city was the seat of many regimes from the 3rd century CE, among them Eastern Wu, the Eastern Jin and Southern dynasties, the Southern Tang, the early Ming and the Republic of China.

It was destroyed or plundered several times: by the Sui in 589, by the Northern Song in 976, by the Qing in 1864 after the fall of the Taiping capital, and by the Japanese army in 1937, when the Nanjing Massacre began.
When the Yongle Emperor moved the Ming capital to Beijing in 1421 Nanjing became a secondary capital, and it grew into a commercial and cultural city of silk, publishing and examinations.
dyk: The Sultan of Boni died during a state visit to the Ming capital in 1408 and was buried in Nanjing, where the Interpreters Institute housed foreign envoys.
ev: Sun Quan proclaims himself emperor and makes Jianye the capital of Eastern Wu
Sima Rui makes Jiankang his capital, and the Eastern Jin dynasty follows
Emperor Wen of Sui orders Jiankang demolished
Xu Zhigao becomes emperor of the Southern Tang, with Jiangning as capital
Zhu Yuanzhang takes the throne as the Hongwu Emperor and names the city Nanjing
Taiping forces capture the city and make it their capital, Tianjing
The Kuomintang National Government declares Nanjing the national capital
Japanese forces take the city on 13 December and the Nanjing Massacre begins

f.founded: Historical records attribute the first named urban foundations in the area to the 5th century BCE, Yuecheng and Yecheng, though their locations and dates are debated; Sun Quan moved his headquarters to Moling in 211 and built the Stone City, and made it his capital in 229.
f.where: On the lower Yangtze River in the Yangtze River Delta, in the south-western corner of Jiangsu province, China, with the Qinhuai River running through the main urban area and the Ningzheng Ridge round its north, east and south sides.
f.known: Capital of Eastern Wu, the Eastern Jin, the Southern dynasties, the Southern Tang, the early Ming and the Republic of China; Jiankang's Buddhist monasteries; the Ming city wall and Xiaoling mausoleum; the Taiping capital Tianjing; the Treaty of Nanking; the Nanjing Massacre of 1937–1938
f.today: Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu province and a sub-provincial city of the People's Republic of China, with about 9.4 million people.
